title: Binary Tree Right Side View
prompt:
Return the values visible from the right side of the tree, top to bottom — i.e. the last node of each level.

**Example**: `[1,2,3,null,5,null,4]` → `[1,3,4]`.

Level-order BFS: within each level, grab the value of the final node.

tests.note: deepest-right comes from the left subtree

hints: Standard BFS with the frozen-`size` trick per level.
The right-side value is the node polled when `i == size - 1`.
Still offer both children left-then-right so the last one polled is genuinely the rightmost.

solution.explanation: O(n). Since children are enqueued left→right, the last node dequeued in each level is the rightmost visible one. The `[1,2,3,4]` test proves the answer isn't always the right child — the deepest level's only node comes from the left.
